title: C:metabolic-cell attempt (IBMED, flow-lenia): food-eating Flow-Lenia gliders in their own set-point shell divide to generation 5, the shell speeds them up, and a freshly divided daughter whose food is cut dies while its sister and fed twin persist
summary: fl_forager (matter built only from a conserved, diffusing food field) plus a shell channel S grown where a ring-convolved body density hits a set point and fed back on the matter's growth field through a disk kernel (r-two56's k4/k5 pair). In 3 seeds each glider carries a closed S ring at 9 px (S 0.34-0.40 vs <=0.034 inside and <=0.025 outside; median closure 24/24 sectors), bodies divide to generation 5 (merge/split ~0.85) and glide up to 15-17 body lengths; without the feedback (h5=0) they are slower (median speed 0.39-0.51 vs 0.55-0.81). At a fresh division a food cut that follows one daughter kills it (below 10% of its matter 80-560 t after the fork on 5/6 seeds, 12% on the sixth) while its sister grows 1.8-3.8x and divides and the same daughter in the fed twin persists.

claims.statement: In world.py the gliders grown from one noise patch each carry a closed S shell at 9 px that makes them faster, divide to generation 5 (3 seeds), and a freshly divided daughter whose own food is cut dies while its sister and its fed twin persist (6 seeds).
claims.track: seed 3 fork (forks300/df3.png, forks600/dl3.png): two shelled daughters of a division 18 px apart at t=185; in the fed twin the + daughter glides on in its shell; in the cut run it shrinks and is gone by t~265 while the x sister grows 3.8x and divides

controls_run.B: control_h5_0/seed0-2 (same world and seeds without the shell feedback): slower, fewer travelling tracks (speedcmp.json); shell off = no S
controls_run.E: forks300/ and forks600/: fed twin from the identical fork state vs a food cut following one daughter, 6 seeds
